observation.visible_scene: A square green plastic lid/tray rests on a white surface (dark vent slats visible beneath its lower edge), set against a pale wall. On the tray sits a thick, pale-yellow viscous blob with a notch cut into its left side, surrounded by scattered small white droplets and a thin glossy liquid film; bright elongated reflections streak across the tray surface.
visible_changes: The pale-yellow blob stays in the same position throughout (no translation); only its edges and the surrounding liquid change subtly.
The white liquid pooling in the left notch and along the lower-left rim of the blob gradually widens, drawing out a thin trailing stream toward the lower-left.
The scattered white droplets at the bottom and right of the blob merge/grow slightly as the surrounding film spreads.
The change is slow and continuous across the whole excerpt, indicating an already-ongoing spreading/flowing process rather than a start or stop.
The camera is essentially static: the wall scratch and tray edges hold constant frame positions; the bright streaks are reflections on the glossy tray, not separate moving objects.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the substance is and what causes the slow flow.
Whether the spreading continues, halts, or reverses after the last frame.
The state of the blob before t=0 (the clip begins mid-process).
uncertain_details: Exact material identity of the yellow mass and white droplets.
Whether minor edge shifts reflect true melting/flow or only settling/reflection changes.
Any sub-pixel camera jitter versus real motion is indistinguishable at this sampling rate.
